To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the changes in plasma concentrations of ionised calcium, inorganic phosphate and 1, 25 dihydroxycholecalcifol (1, 25 (OH) 2 D3) associated with egg formation are absent in hens that lay shell-less eggs, demonstrating their direct link to shell calcification.

suppression of shell formation in laying hens has no effect on the variations in the plasma concentration of the gonadal hormones, but does suppress the variations in the concentration of the plasma minerals and hormones whose concentration changes during the formation of a shell.
the changes in the concentrations of ionized Ca2+, inorganic P, 1,24,25-dihydoxycholecalcifero and gonadal hormones during the ovulatory cycle are directly associated with shell calcification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of calcium and phosphorus metabolism in the domestic hen.
the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the calcium metabolism during the laying cycle.
the effects of the laying of hard or shell-less eggs on the plasma levels of the following: calcium, inorganic phosphate, 1, 25 dihydroxy cholecalciferol (D3) and gonadal hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
shell-less eggs were not produced in hens laying normal eggs, and the production of shell-less egg was not associated with the normal cycle of gonadal hormone secretion.
the increase in 1, 25 (OH)2D 3 production in the hen ovary is a result of the high demands of shell formation, and not a direct consequence of the gonadal hormones.
the production of shell-less egg is not a physiological process and that it is not a normal part of the hen's reproductive cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the changes in the blood levels of ionized and total calcium, inorganic P and 1, 25-dihydroxycalciferol associated with egg formation are absent in hens producing shell-less eggs, demonstrating the link between these changes and shell calcification.

the increase in the plasma concentration of 1, 25-(OH) 2D3 during egg formation is a direct consequence of the increased calcium demand of the shell-forming tissues and is probably not under the control of gonadal hormones.
the increase of 1,α-hydroxylase activity and of the plasma 1,25(OH)2D3 concentration at the onset of the ovulatory cycle in hens is not controlled by the gonadal steroid hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shell-less eggs are produced by hens with no changes in the concentrations of the blood minerals and gonadal hormones whose concentrations change in normal hens during egg formation.
the increases in plasma 1,25(OH)2D3 concentrations which occur at the time of ovulation are directly related to the demands for calcium made by shell formation.
the increases in the plasma concentrations in calcium and 1, 25-(OH) 2D 3 associated with the onset of egg formation are not under gonadal control.
